newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bond trading is light, ON funds at 12.75 pct.
newsitem.headline: Greek bond trading is light, ON funds at 12.75 pct.

text.p: Greek overnight funds were trading around 12.75 percent but other shorts were hugging the 13.40 percent in early dealing. Secondary bond trading was subdued, partly blamed on aggressive pricing at Friday's auction, dealers said.
"The market is more liquid today with overnight trades around 12.75 percent but tomnext and longer periods up to a month are hugging 13.40 percent," said a dealer at a state bank.
Secondary bond trading was subdued at opening with traders characterising Friday's auction pricing very aggressive.

"It looks as if the FRNs and the bonds have been unequally distributed with many banks getting a small piece of the cake and institutionals who seek high first-year yields a bigger chunk of FRNs," said a bond trader.
The trader added that interbank funding was too high to justify the auction prices and those who bought the three-year bonds were bound to suffer losses for one-year.
"Apparently they were taking a longer view of the economy and the market and foreign players are the prime suspects," he said. "Overall the ball is in the central bank's court now."
The average accepted bid was 100.361 for the seven-year floaters and 99.823 for the three-year coupon bond. The stop out was at 100.303 for the FRNs and 99.550 for the bond.
Greece auctioned about 200 billion drachmas worth of seven-year FRNs with the first coupon at 13.40 percent, the 12-month T-bill rate set at 12 percent and the spread at 10 basis points last Friday.
It also auctioned 100 billion drachmas of three-year, 11 percent coupon bonds on November 12.
The mark was quoted at 157.38/43 drachmas from Friday's 157.820 fix, the dollar at 238.28/38 drachmas from 236.900 and the Ecu at 303.30/40 from 303.360 drachmas.
